title: RAW co-falling does not establish identity when its predicted injury is denied
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_EXECUTED. Megenberg preserves the report of stones falling with thunder while rejecting thunder-as-stone through expected wounds versus claimed unwounded but blackened victims, then supplies a hot-vapour cause. Keep reported belief, counterfactual consequence, observation scope and alternative explanation distinct.

design.mechanism: The source reports an identity inference from co-occurrence: people think thunder is a stone because a stone often falls with it during severe weather. The author retains that stated co-falling premise but rejects identity through a counterfactual consequence: if thunder were a stone, those it kills would be wounded like victims of other falling stones. The claimed observation instead gives human victims without wounds but blackened at the strike. Hot vapour burning the victims and the blood in their hearts is offered as an alternative cause of unwounded suffocation.
design.contrast: R1: co-falling proves that the thunder and stone are one entity. R2: rejection of identity denies that stones ever fall with thunder. R3: no wounds means no harm or no death. R4: the alternative burning explanation is the belief attributed to people, while the author endorses the stone explanation. R5: the human observation is silently widened into an observed census of humans and beasts. R6: the proposed vapour account is treated as medically established merely because the author rejects the stone account.
design.prediction: A faithful content account preserves the co-occurrence while rejecting the identity inference, and keeps the expected wound consequence under the stone hypothesis distinct from the reported absence of wounds. Blackening and death require the stated alternative explanation rather than being erased as harmlessness. Swapping author commitment and reported belief, negating co-falling instead of identity, or turning no wounds into survival changes the argument. Merely naming thunder, stone, wound and heart does not reproduce this inferential structure.
whole_source_duties: Exact local scope92.11 beginning iedoch sint läut through92.20 ending erstickent si ân wunden; the following ez kêrt auch der mensch begins a separate face-turning account.
The belief is attributed to people; the stone often falls with thunder in great weather. Co-falling is the stated ground of the belief, not independently verified evidence here.

The counterfactual predicts wounds in people AND animals killed by the proposed stone, compared with other falling stones. The subsequent we-see claim explicitly mentions people, not a separately reported animal case.

The reported human victims are unwounded but black at the strike. They are killed/suffocated; absence of wounds must not become absence of injury or death. The source distinguishes blackening from wunden; do not erase that written category distinction through a modern broad definition of injury.

Hot vapour burns them and the blood in the heart; therefore they suffocate without wounds. This historical physiology is the authorial alternative, not a modern medical finding or a formally established exhaustive disjunction.

The preceding92.1–11 sensory-absence explanation, following92.20–23 face-turning and92.23–30 material-selective damage remain whole-chapter context. Do not recruit them as new observations proving the stone argument.

The rest of the complete chapter retains its formation, perception, analogies, bodily effects, warning objection, wine, seasonal and final classification claims. This card preserves one contiguous argument, not a whole-chapter translation or renamed recipient-damage offer.
